newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-SINGSPIEL A MAJESTIC CORONATION CUP WINNER.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-SINGSPIEL A MAJESTIC CORONATION CUP WINNER.

text.p: Globetrotting world champion Singspiel on Friday spreadeagled a class field to land the Coronation Cup with majestic ease.

"He gives me goosepimples when I ride him," said ebullient Frankie Dettori after the 5-4 favourite swept to an effortless five-length victory over 9-2 chance Dushyantor with French 14-1 shot Le Destin half a length back in third.
Dettori, given a rousing cheer after his trademark flying dismount afterwards, said: "It is good for racing to have a horse like this. He is a hero and a champion.
"What a horse, he is beautiful," Dettori said of the resilient Singspiel who has also plundered two of the world's richest races -- the Japan Cup and the Dubai World Cup.

Sheikh Mohammed, whose tough colt has now won more than five million dollars around the world from Toronto to Tokyo, was uncharacteristically effusive after Singspiel's impressive charge around the unique Epsom switchback.

"He has been around the world to win his races and he is stronger this year," he said of the colt who will be now aimed at Ascot's King George VI Stakes, the Prix de L'Arc de Triomphe in Paris and then the Breeders' Cup in the United States.
Trainer Michael Stoute was glowing with pride after Singspiel's first Group One win in England in his peripatetic career.
It was a tremendous confidence booster for the Stoute stable's Entrepreneur, odds-on favourite for Saturday's Epsom Derby.
Both Detttori and Sheikh Mohammed hailed Singspiel as a real international star of the track and just what the sport needs.

"The public likes them because they get to know them over the years. Singspiel is a good-looking horse and has an Arabic look to his face," Dubai's defence minister and the world's most powerful racing owner said.
Dettori, racing's most popular jockey since Lester Piggott, was almost lost for words to describe Singspiel.
He stuck mostly to staccato superlatives: "What a horse. He is beautiful. He is fantastic."
And there was no doubting the pleasure Singspiel gave Dettori who said: "I was smiling all the way through the final furlong."
